POPULATION.corpus_view: rules-src/checks/<ORG>/*.yaml — AUTHORED view, 1 file == 1 rule id. NOT rules/ (shipped, per package), NOT rules-legacy/.
POPULATION.population_b_definition: UNCHANGED from d3-population-b-census.py — deliberately not redefined, so the partition stays comparable to the predecessor's 443.

qualifier_classes.definition: per (rule, declared dataset, column, role) read — what the leaf-name qualifier actually denotes

SELF_IN_SCOPE_reported_not_applied.meaning: census.classify_shape tests RELREC and '--' BEFORE `name in own`, so a Match_Datasets entry naming the rule's OWN primary is classified foreign. REPORTED ONLY — applying it would change Population B.

resolution.granularity: QUAD (rule, resolved dataset, column, role), NON_COLUMN_CLASSES excluded — they are not column reads, so 'unresolved' does not apply

tree_mask_effect.definition: over-fire SITES the leaf criterion accepts but the whole-Check tri-state evaluation rejects — the Check ANDs a FALSE_ON_NULL leaf (non_empty / exists / is_contained_by / …) on the SAME operand in front of the negative leaf, so the rule provably cannot fire.

T5_caused_only_by_non_column_reads.meaning: T5 says 'nothing resolved'. For these rules nothing resolved because their only foreign read is NOT a column read at all (a metadata field). ⚠ They are not 'unknown' — they read no foreign COLUMN.

T5_with_no_extracted_read_at_all.meaning: the rule declares a foreign dependency but no column read could be extracted from it (e.g. an Operations entry with neither name nor names nor group nor filter, and no Match_Datasets keys)
